questions.q: True or false? Blue's two strikers can press all three of our backs at once.
questions.explain: Right, it's false. Two pressers can reach only two backs, so one of our backs stays free.
choiceExplanations: Count them: two strikers against three backs. One back is always left free.
Right, it's false. Two pressers can reach only two backs, so one of our backs stays free.

questions.q: The keeper has the ball behind the new press. What happens next?
options: Keeper passes to the right back
Keeper kicks long to our striker
questions.explain: Yes. The left back is free now, so Blue's strikers must turn and chase again.
choiceExplanations: Blue's midfielder now presses the right back, so that pass walks into pressure.
A long kick usually gives the ball away. A free back is much closer.
Yes. The left back is free now, so Blue's strikers must turn and chase again.

questions.q: Now the strikers press our centre back and right back. Which pass finds the free back?
options: Pass to the right central midfielder
questions.explain: Right. Both strikers are on the right, so the left back is the one they cannot reach.
choiceExplanations: A striker is pressing the right back, so that pass is under pressure.
Right. Both strikers are on the right, so the left back is the one they cannot reach.
Blue's midfielders are close to him, so the pass could be cut out.
